BC ⟂ EE₁ : Proved [10]


# Proof:

000. | AC = CE [C0], BE = BD [C1] =(AR Deduction)> CE = BE [0]
001. | CE = BE [0], B, C, E are not collinear [N0] =(r13 Isosceles triangle equal angles)> ∠(BC,BE) = ∠(CE,BC) [1]

004. | F is the circumcenter of the circle ●BCE [C2] =(r72 Disassembling a circle)> BF = EF [4]

006. | F is the circumcenter of the circle ●BCE [C2], E₁ is the midpoint of BC [C3] =(r17 Central angle vs inscribed angle I)> ∠(BE,CE) = ∠(E₁F,CF) [6]
007. | ∠(BC,BF) = ∠(CF,BC) [3], ∠(BE,BF) = ∠(EF,BE) [5], ∠(BE,CE) = ∠(E₁F,CF) [6] =(AR Deduction)> E₁F ∥ EF [7]
008. | E₁F ∥ EF [7] =(r28 Overlapping parallels)> E, E₁, F are collinear [8]
009. | E, E₁, F are collinear [8] =(r82 Parallel from collinear)> EE₁ ∥ EF [9]
010. | ∠(BC,BE) = ∠(CE,BC) [1], EE₁ ∥ EF [9] =(AR Deduction)> BC ⟂ EE₁ [10]


# Appendix: AR deductions:



000. | Ratio Chasing to prove CE = BE:
| Premise AC = CE gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise BE = BD gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
We are left with a linear equation with coefficients {} that gives CE = BE



007. | Angle Chasing to prove E₁F ∥ EF:
| Premise ∠(BC,BF) = ∠(CF,BC) gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise ∠(BE,BF) = ∠(EF,BE) gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise ∠(BE,CE) = ∠(E₁F,CF) gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
We are left with a linear equation with coefficients {} that gives E₁F ∥ EF



010. | Angle Chasing to prove BC ⟂ EE₁:

| Premise EE₁ ∥ EF gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
We are left with a linear equation with coefficients {} that gives BC ⟂ EE₁

# Goals

AO₁ = AO₂ : Proved [15]


# Proof:

000. | O₂ is the circumcenter of the circle ●ABH [C0] =(r72 Disassembling a circle)> AO₂ = BO₂ [0]
001. | AO₂ = BO₂ [0], A, B, O₂ are not collinear [N0] =(r13 Isosceles triangle equal angles)> ∠(AB,AO₂) = ∠(BO₂,AB) [1]
002. | O₁ is the circumcenter of the circle ●ABC [C1] =(r72 Disassembling a circle)> AO₁ = CO₁ [2]
003. | AO₁ = CO₁ [2], A, C, O₁ are not collinear [N1] =(r13 Isosceles triangle equal angles)> ∠(AC,AO₁) = ∠(CO₁,AC) [3]
004. | O₂ is the circumcenter of the circle ●ABH [C0] =(r72 Disassembling a circle)> AO₂ = HO₂ [4]
005. | AO₂ = HO₂ [4], A, H, O₂ are not collinear [N2] =(r13 Isosceles triangle equal angles)> ∠(AH,AO₂) = ∠(HO₂,AH) [5]
006. | O₁ is the circumcenter of the circle ●ABC [C1] =(r72 Disassembling a circle)> CO₁ = BO₁ [6]
007. | CO₁ = BO₁ [6], B, C, O₁ are not collinear [N3] =(r13 Isosceles triangle equal angles)> ∠(BC,BO₁) = ∠(CO₁,BC) [7]
008. | A, B, D are collinear [C2], AD = BD [C3] =(r54 Definition of midpoint)> D is the midpoint of AB [8]
009. | O₁ is the circumcenter of the circle ●ABC [C1], D is the midpoint of AB [8] =(r17 Central angle vs inscribed angle I)> ∠(AC,BC) = ∠(AO₁,DO₁) [9]
010. | O₂ is the circumcenter of the circle ●ABH [C0], D is the midpoint of AB [8] =(r17 Central angle vs inscribed angle I)> ∠(AH,BH) = ∠(DO₂,BO₂) [10]
011. | ∠(AC,BC) = ∠(AO₁,DO₁) [9], ∠(AH,BH) = ∠(DO₂,BO₂) [10] =(AR Deduction)> DO₁ ∥ DO₂ [11]
012. | DO₁ ∥ DO₂ [11] =(r28 Overlapping parallels)> D, O₁, O₂ are collinear [12]
013. | D, O₁, O₂ are collinear [12] =(r82 Parallel from collinear)> O₁O₂ ∥ DO₁ [13]
014. | ∠(AB,AO₂) = ∠(BO₂,AB) [1], ∠(AC,AO₁) = ∠(CO₁,AC) [3], ∠(AH,AO₂) = ∠(HO₂,AH) [5], ∠(BC,BO₁) = ∠(CO₁,BC) [7], O₁O₂ ∥ DO₁ [13] =(AR Deduction)> ∠(AO₁,O₁O₂) = ∠(O₁O₂,AO₂) [14]
015. | ∠(AO₁,O₁O₂) = ∠(O₁O₂,AO₂) [14], A, O₁, O₂ are not collinear [N4] =(r14 Equal base angles imply isosceles)> AO₁ = AO₂ [15]


# Appendix: AR deductions:



011. | Angle Chasing to prove DO₁ ∥ DO₂:

| Premise ∠(AH,BH) = ∠(DO₂,BO₂) gives a linear equation with coefficients {}

014. | Angle Chasing to prove ∠(AO₁,O₁O₂) = ∠(O₁O₂,AO₂):
| Premise ∠(AB,AO₂) = ∠(BO₂,AB) gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise ∠(AC,AO₁) = ∠(CO₁,AC) gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise ∠(AH,AO₂) = ∠(HO₂,AH) gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise ∠(BC,BO₁) = ∠(CO₁,BC) gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise O₁O₂ ∥ DO₁ gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
We are left with a linear equation with coefficients {} that gives ∠(AO₁,O₁O₂) = ∠(O₁O₂,AO₂)

End of proof.
